posts.cooked:
Sorry if this was already asked, but I don't remember seeing it.  So on it's "villain" side the heriloom increases Kismet's damage by the number of Jinxes in play.  Both Imminent Destruction and Unlucky Break are one-shot Jinxes that deal damage.  So is the damage she deals from these cards effectively +1 because they are in-play while resolving?

My guess is yes, because putting a one-shot "into play" makes it resolve, so I would assume it stays "in play" until done.

posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked:
Unlucky Break would not get the bonus because it only deals damage if a hero has the Talisman, and thus Kismet does not, ergo she doesn't increase her damage for Jinxes in play.  Imminent Destruction, though, seems like it would benefit if she has the Talisman while it resolves.  Makes sense, after all, since she's probably supposed to be using the Talisman to cause the Destruction, even though she can do it without the thing.

(Still, I think this is one place where MTG's concept of "reminder text" would come in extremely handy.)
